Σαλμών.long: Salmon, son of Nahshon and father of Boaz.
Σαλμών.as:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן),
Salmon: Mt 1:4, 5, Lk 3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†

Σαδώκ.as:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, v. supr., s.v. Σαδδουκαῖος)
Sadoc, Zadok: Mt 1:14.†

Σαδδουκαῖος.long: a Sadducee, a member of the aristocratic party among the Jews, from whom the high-priests were almost invariably chosen.
Σαδδουκαῖος.sd: a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite
Σαδδουκαῖος.as:
Σαδδουκαῖος, -ου, ὁ
(< Heb. צָדוֹק, II Ki 15:24, al.),
a Sadducee (cf. Swete, Mk., 277): Mt 3:716:1, 6, 11, 1222:23, 34, Mk 12:18, Lk 20:27, Ac 4:15:1723:6-8.†

Σατανᾶς.der: of Chaldee origin corresponding to H04566 (with the definite affix);
Σατανᾶς.as:
Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ
(so also Sir 21:30, but in III Ki 11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb.שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό,
Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. c.): Mt 4:1012:26, Mk 1:133:23, 264:15, Lk 10:1811:1813:1622:3, 31, Jo 13:27, Ac 5:326:18, Ro 16:20, I Co 5:57:5, II Co 2:1111:14, I Th 2:18, II Th 2:9, I Ti 1:205:15, Re 2:9, 13, 243:912:920:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Mt 16:23Mk 8:33; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, II Co 12:7.†

σαλπίζω.sd: to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively)
σαλπίζω.as:
σαλπίζω
[in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;]
to sound a trumpet: Re 8:6 ff.9:1, 1310:711:15; metaph., Mt 6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: I Co 15:52.†

σαπρός.as:
** σαπρός, -ά -όν
[in Sm.: Le 27:14, 33 * ;]
rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opp. to ἀγαθός, καλός), Mt 7:17, 1812:33Lk 6:43; of fish, Mt 13:48.
Metaph., in moral sense: λόγος σ., Eph 4:29. "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†

Σαμαρίτης.sd: a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria
Σαμαρίτης.as:
Σαμαρείτης
(-ίτης, Τ; v. WH, App., 154; Bl., § 3, 4), -ου, ό,
a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (v.s. Σαμαρία): Mt 10:5, Lk 9:5210:3317:16, Jo 4:9, 39, 40, Ac 8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jo 8:48.†

σαλεύω.long: I shake, excite, disturb in mind, stir up, drive away.
σαλεύω.sd: to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite
σαλεύω.kj: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up
σαλεύω.as:
σαλεύω
(< σάλος), [in LXX for מוּט, נוּעַ, etc. ;]
prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mt 11:7, Lk 7:24; a house, Lk 6:48, Ac 4:3116:26; the earth, He 12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:25, Lk 21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Lk 6:38. Metaph.,
(a)to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., He 12:27;
(b) c. acc pers., to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: Ac 2:25(LXX);
(c)to unsettle or drive away: pass., seq. ἀπὸ τ. νοός, II Th 2:2;
(d)to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Ac 17:13.†

σάκκος.sd: "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief)
σάκκος.as:
σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ
(cf. Heb.שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),
1.a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Re 6:12.
2. Anything made of sackcloth;
(a)a sack (Ge 42:25, al.);
(b)a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13, Re 11:3.†

σάββατον.sd: the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications
σάββατον.as:
† σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά
[in LXX for שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּתוֹן ;]
1.the seventh day of the week, the sabbath
(a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: Mt 12:8, Mk 2:27, Lk 6:5, al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, Ex 20:8, al., usually τῶν σ., v. infr.), Lk 13:1614:5; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, Ac 1:12 (cf. Mt 24:20); dat., of time (τῷ) σ., Lk 6:914:1; ἐν (τῷ) σ., Mt 12:2, Lk 6:7, Jo 5:16, al.; acc., of duration, τὸ σ., Lk 23:56; κατὰ πᾶν σ., Ac 13:2715:2118:4; pl., σ. τρία, Ac 17:2 R, txt. (but v. infr.);
(b) as most freq. in LXX (v. Swete, Mk., 17; Thackeray, Gr., 35) the pl. form, τὰ σ. (v. supr. on the Aram. form. There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): Mt 28:1, Col 2:16; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. (Ex 20:8, al.), Lk 4:16, Ac 13:1416:13; dat. pl. (in LXX -τοις, but I Mac 2:38 as in NT) by metaplasmus (Bl., § 9, 3), σάββασι, Mt 12:1, 5, 10-12Mk 1:212:233:2, 4, Lk 4:316:2.
2.seven days, a week;
(a) the sing. form: πρώτη σαββάτσυ, Mk 16:9; δὶς τοῦ σ. (Bl., § 35, 4; 36, 13), Lk 18:12; κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου, I Co 16:2; pl., σ. τρία, Ac 17:2 R, mg. (but v. supr.);
(b) the pl. form: ἡ μία τῶν σ. (where the gen. = μετὰ τά; Soph., Lex., 43a), Mt 28:1, Mk 16:2, Lk 24:1, Jo 20:1, 19, Ac 20:7

σαρόω.sd: akin to G4951 (σύρω)); meaning a broom; to sweep
σαρόω.der: from a derivative of (to brush off;
σαρόω.as:
* σαρόω, -ῶ
late form of σαίρω,
to sweep: c. acc, Lk 15:8; pass., Mt 12:44, Lk 11:25.†

σάτον.long: a large measure equal to nearly three English gallons.
σάτον.sd: a certain measure for things dry
σάτον.as:
† σάτον, -ου, τό
(Aram. סָאתָא = Heb.סְאָה), [in LXX: Hg 2:17 (16) * ;]
a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mt 13:33, Lk 13:21.†

σαγήνη.der: from a derivative of (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope);
σαγήνη.as:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶם ;]
a drag-net, seine: Mt 13:47.†
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (q.v.), δίκτυον

σάρξ.long: flesh, body, human nature, materiality; kindred.
σάρξ.sd: flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such)
σάρξ.der: probably from the base of G4563 (σαρόω);
σάρξ.as:
σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]
flesh;
1. as in cl. generally,
(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: I Co 15:39, II Co 12:7, Ga 6:13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, I Co 5:50; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Lk 24:39; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Re 17:1619:18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. c. (cf. κατεσθίειν, IV Ki 9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, freq. in l.); metaph., Ja 5:3; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, Jo 6:52-56;
(b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: Ac 2:26(LXX), 31, II Co 12:7, Ga 4:14, Eph 5:29; μία σ., Mk 10:8; εἰς σ. μίαν (Ge 2:24), Mt 19:5, Mk 10:8, I Co 6:16, Eph 5:31; hence, of the material as opp. to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opp. to πνεῦμα, I Co 5:5, II Co 7:1, Col 2:5, I Pe 3:18, 4:6; to ψύχη, Ac 2:31, Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Ro 7:5, Ga 2:20, Phl 1:22, 24I Pe 4:2; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, He 5:7; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Ga 6:12, 13, Phl 3:3, 4.
2. As in Heb. idiom,
(a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., § 47, 9), Mt 24:22, Mk 13:20, I Pe 1:24; esp. of man and his mortality (Ps 55 (56):5, Si 28:5, al.), Jo 1:14; πᾶσα σ. (v. supr.), Lk 3:6, Jo 17:2, Ac 2:17, ἐν σ., I Jo 4:2, I Ti 3:16;
(b) of natural origin and relationship (Ge 2:24, Is 58:7, al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., Ro 9:8; κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, I Co 10:18, Ga 4:23, 29; ἡ σ. μου, Ro 11:14 (cf. Jg 9:2, II Ki 5:1, al.).
3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),
(a) without any ethical disparagement: Ro 7:1813:14; opp. to πνεῦμα, Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., Jo 1:13; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., I Jo 2:16; pl., II Pe 2:18; παθεῖν σαρκί, I Pe 4:1;
(b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opp. to νοῦς, Ro 7:25; to πνεῦμα, Ro 8:4-9, 12, 13, Ga 5:16, 17, 196:8 (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844 ff.).

σάλπιγξ.long: a trumpet, the sound of a trumpet.
σάλπιγξ.der: perhaps from G4535 (σάλος) (through the idea of quavering or reverberation);
σάλπιγξ.as:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;]
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: I Co 14:8, He 12:19, Re 1:104:18:2, 6, 139:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mt 24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, I Th 4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., I Co 15:52.†

σαβαχθάνι.sd: thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress
σαβαχθάνι.der: of Chaldee or (H07662 with pronominal suffix);
σαβαχθάνι.as:
† σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.c., WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי),
sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 (Ps 21 (22):2, Heb. עֲוַבְתָּנִי).†

σανδάλιον.sd: of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad
σανδάλιον.as:
σανδάλιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Jos 9:5, Is 20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, q.v.), Jth 10:416:9 * ;]
a sandal: Mk 6:9, Ac 12:8.†

Σαλώμη.long: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the apostles.
Σαλώμη.der: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H07965);
Σαλώμη.as:
Σαλώμη, -ης, ἡ
(< Heb. שָׁלוֹם),
Salome: Mk 15:4016:1.†

Σαλά.long: Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus.
Σαλά.as:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שָׁלַח),
Sala, Shalah: Lk 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, q.v.), ib. 35.†

Σάρεπτα.long: Zarephath, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.
Σάρεπτα.sd: Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine
Σάρεπτα.as:
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת),
Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Lk 4:26.†

Σαμάρεια.long: Samaria, a small district of Palestine, bounded by Galilee on the north, and by Judaea on the south, and taking its name from the city of Samaria, the ancient capital of the kingdom of (northern) Israel.
Σαμάρεια.sd: Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine

σάλος.g: the tossing of the sea in a tempest
σάλος.long: the tossing of the sea in a tempest; agitation, rolling.
σάλος.der: probably from the base of G4525 (σαίνω);
σάλος.as:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;]
in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Lk 21:25.†

Σαλείμ.der: probably from the same as G4531 (σαλεύω);
Σαλείμ.as:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl.,
Salim: Jo 3:23 (v. Westc., in l.; DB, iii, 354).†

Σαμαρῖτις.sd: a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria
Σαμαρῖτις.as:
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, v. supr.), -ιδος, ἡ
1. in FlJ (B.J., I, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria.
2.a Samaritan woman: Jo 4:9.†

Σαμουήλ.as:
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb.שְׁמוּאֵל),
Samuel (I Ki 1:20, al.): Ac 3:2413:20, He 11:32.†

Σάπφιρα.long: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian.

Σαῦλος.sd: Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul
Σαῦλος.der: of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549 (Σαούλ);
Σαῦλος.as:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, q.v.),
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Ac 7:588:1, 39:1, 8, 11, 22, 2411:25, 3012:2513:1, 2, 7, 9.†

Σαούλ.long: Saul, (a) the first king of Israel, (b) the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles.
Σαούλ.sd: Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul
Σαούλ.as:
Σαούλ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb.שָׁאוּל)
Saul;
(a) the King of Israel: Ac 13:21;
(b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): Ac 9:4, 1722:7, 1326:14.†

Σαρών.long: Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa.
Σαρών.sd: Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine
Σαρών.as:
Σάρων, -ωνος (acc -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן),
the plain of Sharon: Ac 9:35.†

Σαλαμίς.long: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.
Σαλαμίς.der: probably from G4535 (σάλος) (from the surge on the shore);
Σαλαμίς.as:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνος, ἡ
Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Ac 13:5.†

Σαμοθρᾴκη.long: Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace.
Σαμοθρᾴκη.sd: Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean
Σαμοθρᾴκη.as:
Σαμοθρᾴκη
(-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ
Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Ac 16:11.†

Σάμος.long: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.
Σάμος.sd: Samus, an island of the Mediterranean
Σάμος.as:
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ
Samos, an island in the Ægean: Ac 20:15.†

Σαλμώνη.long: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.
Σαλμώνη.der: perhaps of similar origin to G4529 (Σαλαμίς);
Σαλμώνη.as:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ
Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Ac 27:7.†

σανίς.as:
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ
[in LXX: Ca 8:9, Ez 27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;]
a board, plank: Ac 27:44

Σάρρα.sd: Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham
Σάρρα.as:
Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Ge 17:15),
Sarah: Ro 4:199:9, He 11:11, I Pe 3:6.†

σάρκινος.sd: similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft
σάρκινος.as:
σάρκινος, -η, -ον
(< σάρξ), [in LXX: II Ch 32:8, Ez 11:1936:26 (בָּשָׂר), Es 4:17, Pr 24:23 (29:27) * ;]
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; v. Tr., Syn., § lxxii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., v. MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Ro 7:14, I Co 3:1, II Co 3:3, He 7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except II Co, l.c., but the evidence is decisive against it.)†
SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v

Σαβαώθ.sd: armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God
Σαβαώθ.der: of Hebrew origin (H06635 in feminine plural);
Σαβαώθ.as:
† σαβαώθ indecl.,
[in LXX for צְבָאוֺת, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase יהוה צי is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; v. DB, iii, 137 f.) ;]
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (v. DB, l.c.): Ro 9:29(LXX), Ja 5:4.†

σαρκικός.sd: pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate
σαρκικός.as:
* σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (< σάρξ)
(v.l. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7)
= Lat. carnalis, i.e.
(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Ro 15:27, I Co 9:11;
(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, I Pe., 133): I Co 3:3, II Co 1:1210:4, I Pe 2:11.†
SYN.: σάρκινος (q.v.), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ lxxi, lxxii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Ro 7:14

σαργάνη.long: a basket, generally of twisted cords.
σαργάνη.as:
* σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ
1.a plaited rope (Æsch.).
2.a hamper, a basket made of ropes: II Co 11:33.†

σαίνομαι.long: I fawn upon, flatter, beguile; pass: I am perturbed.
σαίνομαι.sd: to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb)
σαίνομαι.as:
* σαίνω
1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
2. Metaph., of persons, c. acc., to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., I Th 3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, v. ICC, and M, Th., in l.).†

σαββατισμός.long: a keeping of the Sabbath, a Sabbath rest.
σαββατισμός.sd: a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven)
σαββατισμός.as:
*† σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath,Ex 16:30, al.),
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaph., as in Mishna (Zorell, s.v.), He 4:9.†

Σαλήμ.sd: Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine

Σαμψών.long: Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.
Σαμψών.as:
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן),
Samson (Jg 13 ff.): He 11:32.†

Σάρδεις.long: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.
Σάρδεις.sd: Sardis, a place in Asia Minor
Σάρδεις.as:
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ
Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Re 1:113:1, 4.†

σάρδιον.sd: sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called
σάρδιον.der: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base;
σάρδιον.as:
σάρδιον, -ον, τό
[in LXX for אֹדֶם, Ex 28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;]
the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Re 4:321:20.†

σαλπιστής.as:
* σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Att. σαλπιγκτής), -οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Re 18:22.†

σάπφιρος.as:
† σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for סַפִּיר ;]
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Re 21:19.†

σαρδόνυξ.long: sardonyx, a precious stone, white streaked with red.
σαρδόνυξ.sd: hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called
σαρδόνυξ.der: from the base of G4556 (σάρδιος) and (the nail of a finger;
σαρδόνυξ.as:
* σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ
(< σάρδιον, ὄνυξ),
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Re 21:20.†
